message.content: {"parent_id":"initial","target_witnesses":["r0_witness_0"],"concept":"Slow input-history memory","explanation":"The witness compares approximately similar x values with u=0 but different preceding input durations. The longer, weaker input history is associated with a less negative estimated derivative. A slowly decaying latent trace of past input could distinguish these cases, whereas the parent model uses only current x and u. This is a candidate explanation, not proof: the states and derivatives are approximate and noisy.","analogy":{"domain":"linear systems","relation":"a first-order low-pass state retains a decaying trace of past forcing","mapping":"z0 is the filtered history of u, with rate u-p0*z0; its contribution to dx/dt is the fitted coefficient on z0","breaks_when":"the input changes much faster than the memory time scale, or when response depends on history features not captured by a single exponentially weighted trace"},"provenance":"model_knowledge_unverified","spec":{"parameters":[{"name":"p0","lower":0.05,"initial":0.25,"upper":1.5}],"states":[{"name":"z0","meaning":"exponentially decaying trace of prior input, initialized to zero","rate":"u-p0*z0"}],"terms":["1","x","u","z0"]},"distinguishing_prediction":"After different-duration input pulses, compare trials at matched x and u=0. This model predicts different instantaneous drift when their residual z0 values differ; the current-state-only parent predicts the same drift. With input held at zero, the memory contribution should decay on a timescale set by 1/p0.","falsifier":"Repeated, adequately resolved trials with matched x and u=0 but substantially different input histories show no reproducible derivative difference, or show differences inconsistent with a decaying filtered-input trace.","limitations":"The supplied witness is an approximate match and does not establish latent memory. A single trace may conflate input history with unmodeled drift or other latent processes; coefficients and the memory timescale require fitting and complete-trajectory validation."}
